The AI Compute Race report prices GPU compute outside the biggest buyers: a three-year commitment cuts the median price by 48%, while 17 of 22 tracked GPU models rose in price over the past year

DALLAS, Texas – November 13, 2026 – Fluence has published The AI Compute Race, a report that prices GPU cloud compute for every company that is not a frontier lab or a hyperscaler. It was produced with research partners NEAR AI, io.net, Boundless, Phala, Gensyn, Fortytwo, Theta, Compute Labs and GAIB. Its central finding: where a company buys a GPU-hour sets the price. Across H100, H200 and B200 models, hyperscalers list GPUs at 1.98 times the GPU-cloud median, from 1.4 times on the B200 to 2.8 times on the H100. The same H200 lists from $4.08 to $10.60 an hour.

Commitment length matters almost as much as provider choice. Against each provider’s own on-demand rate, a one-year reservation cuts the median price by 21% and a three-year term by 48%. Spot capacity lists at 53% of on-demand, for workloads that can be interrupted.

Buyers who expect GPU prices to fall may need to recheck their budgets. Seventeen of the 22 GPU models tracked by GetDeploying cost more than a year earlier, and the median H100 rents for 13% to 30% more, depending on the window measured.

The report also traces why prices are rapidly rising:

“Open-weight models are close behind the best closed ones, and companies are switching to them. Any company with GPUs can now serve a near-frontier model on hardware it controls. The GPUs are the hard part,” said Evgeny Ponomarev, Co-founder of Fluence.

The report closes with four ways to pay less for the same compute: compare the same chip across provider types, commit when the workload is steady, match the GPU generation to the model, and look beyond the hyperscalers, since much of the newest neocloud capacity is contracted to labs years ahead.

The full report is available at fluence.ai/compute-race-2026.

Fluence Cloud is a GPU cloud provider with capacity from independent data centers (fluence.ai). Founded in 2017 by Dmitry Kurinskiy, Evgeny Ponomarev and Tom Trowbridge, the company has raised $14 million from investors including 1KX, Multicoin, Distributed Global, Blockchange, Tiger Global and Protocol Labs.

On November 10, 2026, an official Nadex notice said the exchange certified a swap based on the price of SHIB at a specific time and date. The product, called the Shiba Inu Strike Event Contract, began trading on or after Nov. 13, 2026.

Home » Trendsetter News » Wall Street Trading Booms on Crypto Exchanges. Which Tokens Benefit?

Crypto exchanges are seeing a surge in trading tied to traditional markets, but will token holders benefit most?

Crypto exchanges handled $3.16 trillion in trading tied to stocks, gold, oil and other traditional markets over the period tracked by research cited in a new Firehustle video episode.

The channel’s host, discussing crypto investment themes, argues that the important question is not how much trading these platforms attract, but whether that activity actually benefits HYPE, ONDO and INJ holders.

The figures, attributed to CoinMarketCap research covering 19 exchanges, describe trading exposure to traditional markets, not necessarily purchases of underlying shares. According to Fire Hustle, monthly volume climbed from roughly $100 billion in January to $800 billion in August, with stocks accounting for 62.3% of activity.

The expert identifies Hyperliquid as the closest to strengthening that connection. Trade.XYZ, which operates most of the platform’s traditional-market contracts, reportedly splits trading fees equally with Hyperliquid, whose share largely supports HYPE buybacks.

There is a catch: Trade.XYZ is operating with trading fees discounted by more than 90% to attract users. The YouTube video says those discounts are expected to shrink as markets mature, potentially increasing buyback funding, although higher fees could also change trading behavior.

ONDO presents a different problem. Fire Hustle says Ondo Finance surpassed $4 billion in total value locked, including more than $1.3 billion in tokenized stocks and ETFs, while ONDO holders currently receive no direct fee distributions, buybacks or burns.

A holder-led forum proposal would direct 20% of revenue toward token buybacks and burns, eventually rising to 40%. The host stresses that it is not an approved policy and says the team had not responded.

Crucially, the $4 billion figure represents assets deposited, not revenue available to distribute.

Injective already links application revenue to INJ buybacks and burns, according to the video. But its scale remains modest: the host cites roughly $215 million in traditional-market trading over 30 days and a largest buyback round of about $315,000.

The potential catalyst is Pineapple Prime, a planned mortgage-yield product.

More than $1 billion in mortgage records reportedly moved onto Injective, but the host makes an important distinction: those records are data, not yet money flowing through a live investment product.

In conclusion, these are three way different bets: higher fee capture, an unapproved governance change and a product launch.

None makes trading growth equivalent to token returns, especially when discounted fees, limited activity and concentrated infrastructure can interrupt the connection.

#5140. Tether's Tiny AI Agent Beats Models 2.5 Times Its Size at Controlling Your Phone

Tether's Tiny AI Agent Beats Models 2.5 Times Its Size at Controlling Your Phone

Tether, the company behind the world's largest stablecoin, USDT, is getting surprisingly good at making tiny AI models punch above their weight.

The company on Wednesday unveiled QVAC BotPsy, an 800-million-parameter AI agent designed to carry out everyday tasks on personal devices. Parameters are essentially the knobs that determine how much an AI model can do, and more of them generally translate to improved performance. And for reference, frontier AI models today run in the trillions of parameters.

In the company's own testing, Tether’s relatively tiny model outperformed competitors with up to 2.5 times as many parameters, suggesting that AI assistants may not need enormous models to get things done.

Unlike traditional chatbots that simply respond to questions, BotPsy is agentic, meaning it’s designed to take action. It can identify which tools an application needs, execute commands in the right order, and adjust when something goes wrong.

For example, Tether described a benchmark scenario in which an AI assistant needed to send a message but encountered two problems: Wi-Fi was disabled and the inbox was full. BotPsy turned on Wi-Fi, cleared enough storage, and completed the task, while the underlying model repeatedly attempted the same failed operation.

That's a fairly mundane achievement, but it's precisely the kind of problem that makes AI agents useful outside a chatbot window.

BotPsy is built on Alibaba's Qwen3.5-0.8B architecture, a relatively small language model that Tether trained further to specialize in interacting with software tools. Its 800 million parameters represent the numerical values the model learned during training, and a smaller parameter count generally means less memory is needed to run it.

According to Tether's technical documentation, BotPsy scored 44.0% on BFCL v4, a benchmark that evaluates an AI system's ability to select and execute software functions across different tasks and conversations. Scores reflect a weighted percentage of successful performance across tool-use categories.

The underlying Qwen3.5-0.8B model scored 23.4%, while the considerably larger Qwen3.5-2B reached 37.7%.

BotPsy also scored 58.7% on ACEBench, which evaluates the accuracy of function calls, including selecting the appropriate tools and arguments. Its base model managed 30.1%, while the 2-billion-parameter competitor scored 55.4%.

The company tested five models across six tool-use evaluations, with BotPsy posting the highest results on five. Its average score across those tests reached 45.0%, compared with 38.8% for the larger Qwen model.

BotPsy is the latest addition to QVAC, Tether's effort to build an AI ecosystem that runs on devices controlled by users rather than relying entirely on centralized cloud infrastructure.

The company first introduced QVAC in May 2025, positioning the project as an alternative to AI services operated by technology giants. Its longer-term ambitions included autonomous agents capable of interacting with applications and potentially making payments using Bitcoin and USDT.

Tether expanded that initiative in October 2025 with a 41-billion-token dataset for training science and engineering models, alongside QVAC Workbench, an application that lets users run AI models locally.

Earlier this year, Tether released its SDK, providing developers with tools to build offline AI applications across mobile and desktop operating systems.

The company also developed QVAC MedPsy, a medical AI system designed to run on consumer hardware. Its 1.7-billion-parameter version outperformed Google's much larger MedGemma-27B on HealthBench Hard, a test of realistic clinical conversations evaluated using physician-developed criteria.

BotPsy is currently available as an open-weight model under the Apache 2.0 license, meaning developers can download, modify, and integrate it into their own applications. Tether has also released compressed versions intended to reduce memory requirements for local deployment.

The company has not announced a release date for a finished consumer assistant powered by BotPsy. Its published model card also says the training code and training data are not included in the release.

#5139. XRP Exchange Balances Hit Yearly High, but Long-Term Holders Stay Put

Home » Trendsetter News » XRP Exchange Balances Hit Yearly High, but Long-Term Holders Stay Put

XRP exchange balances have reached a one-year high, while the share of tokens untouched for over a year nears its annual peak.

XRP held on exchanges has reached a one-year high even as the share of coins untouched for more than a year approaches its own annual peak, according to figures cited by wealth-focused commentator Kamilah Stevenson.

Her latest video examines that split following a roughly 10% price decline, arguing that investors’ financial circumstances can matter as much as their market convictions.

Stevenson cites CryptoQuant data showing approximately 11.8 billion XRP on exchanges, the highest balance in a year. That puts more tokens within easy reach of trading, although exchange deposits alone do not establish that holders intend to sell.

Meanwhile, Glassnode figures cited in the video put the share of XRP unmoved for more than a year at roughly 56%, up from 51% in January. Stevenson also says XRP exchange-traded funds still hold about 1.19 billion tokens, despite a small outflow ending a reported 13-week inflow streak.

“Both groups saw the same price,” she says. “They reacted to it in completely opposite ways.”

The contrast is striking, but the metrics have limits. Coins remaining stationary demonstrate inactivity, not necessarily fresh buying or confidence, and neither measure establishes where XRP’s price goes next.

Dr. Stevenson identifies three recurring sources of selling pressure: leverage, investing money needed for near-term expenses, and entering a volatile market without a plan.

She cites roughly $25.7 million in XRP liquidations on Binance during a recent sell-off as an example of positions being closed regardless of investors’ intentions.

Her broader bullish case rests partly on institutional activity involving Ripple and its RLUSD stablecoin.

The YouTube video names Standard Chartered, Cross River Bank and DriveWealth among firms involved in custody, banking or settlement developments.

Those developments should not be treated as equivalent to demand for XRP itself. Nor does institutional infrastructure guarantee that token prices will recover.

The most durable point is about liquidity: cash reserves and manageable exposure reduce the likelihood that an unexpected bill or margin call dictates a sale.

Exchange balances may signal potential selling pressure across the market; they cannot reveal which holders can afford to wait.

#5137. Amazon says no human wrote or reviewed the code for its new cloud testing tool

Human engineers designed the guardrails and release checks. Application security still needs testing on the real cloud.

Amazon released AWS Emulator on Nov. 11, a local tool that imitates AWS services so developers can test cloud applications on their own machines. The company says autonomous AI agents wrote and reviewed its implementation.

In Amazon's engineering account, engineer Matthew Goldberg says his team neither wrote nor reviewed the emulator code. He also describes the substantial engineering work needed to turn an experiment into a product, including the guardrails and checks that determine which changes can ship.

Amazon describes three teams of agents: one manages fidelity tests, another finds differences between the emulator and real AWS, and a third fixes individual issues. Changes face checks for compilation, coding standards, security and regressions before merging, according to the company.

The test agents work from public AWS API models and verify their scenarios against the real cloud. The public evaluation suite says every fidelity test was checked against at least two sandboxed AWS accounts.

AWS calls the degree of agreement with its cloud services “fidelity.” A test passes when the emulator matches AWS for every call in that workflow, including status codes, resulting resources, side effects and errors, according to its fidelity documentation. Returning success where AWS returns an error fails that test.

The boundary is coverage. The evaluation repository explicitly says behavior without a fidelity test is unverified. Passing a scenario establishes a match for that scenario; it does not establish that every way an application uses AWS will work.

Thanks for signing up to The Catalyst. Look out for your first daily email. If you already receive it, you’re all set.

AWS defines a pass within a tested workflow. Untested behavior and application security sit beyond that conclusion.

A passing workflow is evidence for that scenario. It does not validate all AWS behavior or application security.

Diagram shows AWS's pass rule, not a particular test result or measured coverage. Application security still requires testing on real AWS before production.

Qualitative diagram of AWS's published fidelity definition and testing limits. Branches compare the real-AWS reference with emulator replay; they do not represent simultaneous live tests, amounts or coverage proportions.

Diagram shows AWS's pass rule, not a particular test result or measured coverage. Application security still requires testing on real AWS before production.

Security has a separate limit. AWS's security guidance warns against using the emulator to determine whether an application is secure. It does not check AWS KMS key policies or Amazon S3 bucket policies, and a request denied by AWS may succeed locally.

Agent review of implementation security therefore cannot be read as validation of a user's application permissions. The emulator is for building and testing, not production workloads. AWS instructs developers to test their whole application and security settings on real AWS before production.

For builders adopting agent-written software, the release makes the acceptance process as relevant as the code's authorship: which behaviors are checked, what remains outside coverage, and where the developer must still test against the real service.

Cardano founder Charles Hoskinson has doubled down on his comments about completing the blockchain's development. In an AMA, the Cardano founder was asked about finishing Cardano; he answered in the affirmative, saying yes, the roadmap was done.

In a recent livestream titled "Finishing Cardano," Hoskinson maintains that his job with Cardano was done. "My job is done with Cardano," he said, doubling down on his recent statements and on where things stand with Cardano.

Finishing Cardano https://t.co/LtFVLOHrxk

Hoskinson said he saw a barrage of criticism and negative comments after his remarks, with some speculating that he had failed, that Cardano was a failed project, or that he was leaving Cardano. He, however, maintains that there is no ambiguity in his statements.

Hoskinson revisited the launch of Cardano (ADA) in 2015 in response to critics who claimed that he or the Cardano project had failed.

"So, let's look at 2015. There was a crowd sale conducted to sell ADA into Japan. The price for this was less than 0.2 cents per ADA. And Bitcoin was actually used as the settlement system for this. They bought in yen and settled in Bitcoin. So there are even on-chain records of the sales tranche. The total amount of money raised was $72 million."

Highlighting the growth of the Cardano cryptocurrency, Hoskinson noted that the market valuation has increased immensely from an initial $72 million. "We built a network that went from a $72 million valuation to an all-time high of $100 billion," Hoskinson stated.

Cardano reached an all-time high price of $3.09 on September 2, 2021, which corresponded to an all-time-high market capitalization of nearly $100 billion at that peak.

Following ADA's drop from this ATH, Cardano's market valuation sits at $6.03 billion. Hoskinson maintains that this is still growth, up from an initial $72 million. "Even in its deflated state, everybody's saying it's destroyed and it's a dead coin and all these other things. It's $6 billion. It went from 72 to six," Hoskinson said.

Hoskinson specifically reiterated that the Cardano roadmap is not being abandoned and went on to reveal further growth credentials: "We delivered a fully decentralized, recursively self-improving ecosystem. We left behind a community-led and community-owned treasury that, at its all-time high, had $4 billion in value, and initiated a constitution."

"We built an entire on-chain governance system, wrote a constitution, got the entire community involved, and created a recursively self-improving system that's fully decentralized—the most decentralized cryptocurrency on the planet," Hoskinson added.

#5135. Binance Tightens Security With Zero-Knowledge Proof Upgrade

Binance, the world’s largest crypto exchange by volume, has continued to deploy new measures to strengthen security on its exchange after it suffered the biggest cyberattack ever seen in the history of crypto late last month.

In a bid to foster transparency and regain its users' trust, Binance has just announced the completion of a major upgrade to further strengthen its security.

In an announcement shared on November 14, Binance said that it has generated a new zero-knowledge proof for its Proof of Reserves (PoR) system.

According to Binance, the upgrade allows users to independently verify that it holds sufficient assets to cover their account balances on a 1:1 basis.

The exchange further shared snapshots to prove that it maintains reserves above its users' net account balances across six major cryptocurrencies, boosting their confidence in its operating standards.

It also added that the update covers all assets affected by the recent attack, and the exchange showcased its reserves for the following crypto assets: Bitcoin, Ethereum, Tether, BNB, Solana, and USDC.

While withdrawals are being restored in batches, with the last phase scheduled for next week, Binance has continued to improve its operations to replenish all affected assets and tighten security to regain users' trust.

Following its latest move, Binance revealed that its Bitcoin reserves are currently at 100.05%, slightly above the 100% mark. This means that Binance's Bitcoin reserves amount to about 688,283 BTC, substantially above its net user balances of 687,912 BTC.

The case is similar for the rest of the tokens: Ethereum reserves are at 100.02%, while BNB and USDC recorded ratios of 100.39% and 100.07%, respectively.

While Binance also reported stronger reserve ratios for USDT and SOL, at about 104.34% and 105.86%, respectively, it is evident that Binance holds more of these assets than the total amount owed to users.

Binance has specified that the Proof of Reserves covers assets that are in its custody on behalf of users, rather than its entire corporate holdings, assuring users that their funds are fully backed.

#5134. This New AI Music Model Is Already Better Than Suno—We Put ACE to the Test

This New AI Music Model Is Already Better Than Suno—We Put ACE to the Test

Artificial intelligence has gotten pretty good at writing songs. Now, a relatively unfamiliar competitor has managed to beat Suno, arguably the biggest name in AI music, at its own game.

ACE Music v1, developed by ACE Studio, has taken first place on Artificial Analysis' vocal music leaderboard, scoring 1,160 Elo points against Suno v6's 1,144.

The AA-Music-Vocal v1.1 benchmark measures the quality of AI-generated songs containing vocals. Evaluators listen to tracks produced from identical prompts without knowing which model created them, then choose their favorite. Those preferences determine an Elo-style rating, with higher scores indicating stronger listener preference.

The lead is relatively narrow, and the models' statistical confidence intervals overlap. Suno also retains the top position on the separate instrumental music leaderboard.

ACE Studio, founded in 2018, originally focused on synthesizing singing voices from MIDI notes and lyrics. Its latest ACE Music v1 model generates complete songs from written descriptions or user-provided lyrics.

In Decrypt's hands-on tests, ACE Music consistently produced more melodic and coherent songs in mainstream styles.

That said, the vocal performances sounded more natural in general, with fewer of the synthetic artifacts that sometimes make AI singers sound like they're struggling to pronounce their own lyrics, use a lot of autotune or hallucinate words just to fill spaces. (Go ahead and give our song a listen here, which incidentally is about our latest company announcement regarding the Information Exchange.)

ACE also handled song endings better. Where Suno occasionally introduces strange sounds, unnecessary repetitions, hallucinations or abrupt musical changes near the finish, ACE generally maintained its structure and delivered cleaner conclusions.

That matters because making a convincing chorus is relatively easy compared with maintaining a musical idea throughout an entire composition even if the lyrics are already over.

Suno still had an advantage when we pushed the models toward less conventional genres.

In our melodic death metal test, ACE consistently produced tracks featuring a woman singing clearly in a pleasant, clean voice, missing the aggressive vocal delivery expected from the requested style. In general it confuses metal genres all over. Suno offered more creative arrangements in the proper heavy styles, with better stylistic consistency in several similarly demanding prompts.

The results were subjective rather than a controlled benchmark, but they showed why a leaderboard victory doesn't automatically make one model better for every musician.

ACE's most interesting feature may be its songwriting workflow.

Its “Idea” feature can develop a basic concept into lyrics and a structured composition, identifying individual song sections and describing how they should be arranged. Users can then refine the material rather than repeatedly generating completely new tracks.

The v1.1 Preview goes further, creating a musical score before generating audio.

“Each generation is a new performance, so the sound may differ even when the score stays the same,” the developers explain.

Users can edit melodies and chords, regenerate performances, export MIDI files and separate vocals from instruments for further production.

That workflow puts ACE closer to a music production assistant than a simple prompt-to-song application.

The flagship ACE Music v1 model remains closed-source with no public API, so users can only generate via the official site. However, its developers are pursuing a parallel open-source strategy.

ACE Studio and StepFun have already released ACE-Step 1.5, a separate family of models whose code and weights are publicly available. Unlike the proprietary flagship, these can run on users' own hardware—but using a weaker model.

The company also promises another release.

“We plan to open-source ACE Music v1 Flash in late 2026,” the developers state on their website, describing a version designed to balance quality, generation speed and hardware requirements.

ACE Music is available through its browser application, with a limited free tier and paid subscriptions. Commercial usage rights for flagship-model songs require a paid plan, while ACE-Step offers a separate free generation option.

For now, ACE Music v1 holds a 16-point Elo lead over Suno v6 in vocal generation. Its promised Flash release would give local users another model to try before the end of 2026.

#5133. Bitcoin whales turn net long, retailers capitulate as BTC falls to $67K — Rebound coming?

Read the best crypto stories of the day in less than 5 minutes. Join to get it daily in your inbox.

Read the best crypto stories of the day in less than 5 minutes. Join to get it daily in your inbox.

Bitcoin [BTC] closed in the red for the third consecutive day, with its price sliding to $67,000 on the charts. So far, the fall in prices has been driven by both whales and retail traders.

However, this pattern could be changing soon as Bitcoin’s sentiment starts to flip gradually. For instance, Hyperliquid whales turned back to the net long after two weeks of shorting BTC. This was the first selling period for them since March.

In fact, the daily mean of net long and net short grew from -1700 BTC on 8th November to around 900 BTC at press time. This seemed to imply that whales have been buying the dip below $70,000.

During the rally, which started in August, these whales went long. They subsequently sold the top. However, that does not guarantee that they will be right again.

On the other hand, retail traders have been showing signs of capitulation. In fact, BTC’s monthly change in Retail Investor Demand declined to around -10% after a sharp rise to over 17% as the price approached $80,000.

The same is the weakest reading since March. Back then too, Hyperliquid whales were net short on BTC.

This fall in participation by retailers, volumes below $10K, have been common during BTC’s correction.

When looking at historical patterns, it is clearly evident that when retailers capitulate, the prices tend to reverse. Thus, going against the crowd may help investors catch a move, either to the downside or the upside early enough.

Still, that does not mean that the contrarian signal always works. Even though it may be an ideal time to build positions.

Moreover, Bitcoin‘s Open Interest (OI) on Binance fell to $8.30 billion from $9.60 billion in November alone. This was its lowest level since 18th August, when BTC exploded past $65,000.

The slide below $68,000 triggered more long liquidations after those on the previous day. Over the past 24 hours, $1 billion were wiped out in crypto, with longs accounting for $863.3 million against $144.2 million in shorts.

This action forced leveraged traders out as supported by the sharp decline in OI. So, if BTC price stabilizes while OI stays at these levels, it would mean a rebound will be driven more by spot demand than leverage.

Therefore, whale positioning and retail capitulation could be a signal for a sustainable BTC recovery.

However, it needs to be backed by capital inflows from the market in the form of ETFs and spot buying, among others.

#5131. Aave plan could cut some lenders’ share of interest by 60%

Polygon DAI lenders would keep just 30% of borrower interest under the proposal, down from 75%, as Aave’s treasury takes a larger share.

Aave lenders supplying DAI on Polygon could see their share of borrower interest fall from 75% to 30% under a November 12 proposal by TokenLogic. The plan would redirect more interest to Aave’s DAO treasury, with uneven cuts to lender returns across its markets.

The November 12 proposal covers 54 reserves across 12 Aave V3 instances and Ethereum V2. TokenLogic estimates about $4 million in additional annualized DAO revenue using November 9 balances and rates. That total includes roughly $1 million from Plasma USDT0, a change that would enter the formal proposal only once its terms are finalized.

In Aave’s lending system, the mechanism is the reserve factor: the portion of borrower interest allocated to the DAO instead of suppliers. Raising it changes who receives the interest, without directly changing the borrowing-rate curve. TokenLogic argues the larger share would better compensate the DAO for the risks attached to borrowable reserves.

Polygon V3 DAI illustrates how much that allocation can matter. TokenLogic proposes raising its reserve factor from 25% to 70%, with a modeled supply APY reduction of 270 basis points, or 2.70 percentage points. The same line projects $94,373 in additional annual DAO revenue.

With the amount of borrower interest unchanged, suppliers’ share would fall from 75% to 30%. The treasury would receive the difference. In that fixed-input model, the revenue gain comes from a smaller payment to lenders, without requiring more borrowing or a higher price for the same loan.

Polygon DAI illustrates TokenLogic’s November 12 proposal: the interest allocation changes while the model holds borrowing and rates fixed.

The proposed 70% reserve factor leaves suppliers 30% of borrower interest, down from 75%.

Proposal-listed current and proposed factors, not execution evidence. Total borrower interest is held fixed; subsequent liquidity or rate responses can change realized income. The shares concern lending interest, not deposit principal.

Supplier share = 100% minus reserve factor: 100-25=75 and 100-70=30. DAO share rises by 70-25=45 percentage points. Verified with JavaScript arithmetic; bar widths scale linearly to a fixed 600-unit desktop or 312-unit mobile interest pool. This is derived allocation arithmetic, not an APY calculation.

Proposal-listed current and proposed factors, not execution evidence. Total borrower interest is held fixed; subsequent liquidity or rate responses can change realized income. The shares concern lending interest, not deposit principal.

The comparison with other stablecoins shows that the proposal does not apply a uniform yield reduction. TokenLogic models cuts of 173 basis points for Avalanche DAI.e, 78 for Avalanche USDt and 61 for Avalanche USDC. Their proposed reserve factors are 90%, 25% and 25%, respectively.

For savers choosing where to lend stablecoins, those reductions change the return offered for keeping liquidity in the affected reserve. TokenLogic identifies Polygon DAI as a legacy reserve and explicitly uses lower returns as an incentive to move liquidity out of declining markets.

Modeled supply APY changes in TokenLogic’s November 12 proposal using November 9, 2026 balances and rates. Negative values are reductions; 100 basis points equals 1 percentage point. Selected reserves, not the complete proposal.

Source: TokenLogic proposal; model inputs November 9, 2026

A separate Aavescan observation puts the Polygon DAI pool in perspective. Its November 12 midnight-UTC snapshot records 3.30 million DAI deposited, 2.65 million borrowed and a 4.81% supply APR, excluding historical incentives.

Aavescan’s observed APR and TokenLogic’s modeled APY reduction, based on November 9 inputs, describe different rate measures at different dates.

The largest reserve-factor percentages do not necessarily impose the largest yield cuts. TokenLogic proposes 100% factors for selected bitcoin-wrapper and liquid-staking collateral reserves whose lending APYs are already close to zero. Its model puts the lost lending yield in that group at no more than 1 to 2 basis points.

A 100% reserve factor applies to lending interest, not deposit principal. For wstETH, it is also separate from the staking accrual reflected in the token’s stETH value. Redirecting Aave’s incremental lending interest would leave that underlying accrual mechanism intact.

Plasma USDT0 shows why a modest yield cut can still produce a large revenue estimate. TokenLogic models a reserve-factor increase from 5% to 7.5% against about $632 million borrowed. The projected supply APY reduction is 16 basis points, alongside about $1 million in additional annual revenue. Its inclusion remains conditional on finalized Plasma terms.

Even for the other lines, annualizing November 9 balances and rates holds the inputs fixed. The proposal also seeks to change supplier behavior, which could alter those inputs.

For Ethereum V2, TokenLogic proposes raising five remaining borrowed reserves to 99.99%, directing nearly all their interest to the DAO. It expects reduced returns to encourage exits. If suppliers withdraw, utilization could rise and borrowing costs could increase, creating pressure on borrowers to close positions.

Aave’s utilization-based borrowing curve links borrowing costs to how much liquidity is in use. That potential response is separate from changing the curve itself, as in the USDT borrowing-rule update CryptoSlate covered in October.

The November 12 publication lists feedback and escalation to the Aave Improvement Proposal stage as next steps. Its yield cuts and revenue gains remain proposed estimates.

#5130. Bitcoin Short-Term Holders Send $3.6 Billion in BTC to Exchanges at a Loss

Bitcoin Short-Term Holders Send $3.6 Billion in BTC to Exchanges at a Loss

Bitcoin investors who bought recently are moving tens of thousands of coins to cryptocurrency exchanges at a loss, adding to concerns about selling pressure as the cryptocurrency falls toward the low-$70,000 range.

CryptoQuant’s latest short-term holder profit-and-loss chart shows roughly 47,300 BTC transferred to exchanges below their acquisition price over 24 hours, compared with only about 1,100 BTC arriving at a profit.

Combined inflows stood near 48,500 BTC, or around $3.6 billion at Bitcoin’s current price of approximately $74,000.

The research company's chart below shows transfers, not completed sales. Sending Bitcoin to an exchange can be the first step toward selling, but some deposits are made for trading for other tokens, collateral, or other services. The data also does not establish exactly how much of the transferred Bitcoin was subsequently sold.

The distinction is important because the chart measures the behavior of short-term holders, a group that CryptoQuant generally defines as investors holding Bitcoin for less than 155 days.

These are often the buyers most exposed to a sudden price reversal, particularly when their holdings are worth less than they paid.

In a November 11 CryptoQuant analysis, contributor Amr Taha identified two large waves of underwater exchange deposits over the previous week: 50,790 BTC on November 3 and 46,060 BTC on November 10.

“On November 10, profitable transfers stood near 1,700 BTC, meaning approximately 27 BTC arrived at a loss for every 1 BTC transferred at a profit,” Taha wrote.

That is an unusually one-sided flow. Investors moving coins into exchanges are overwhelmingly doing so at prices below those at which they acquired them, rather than cashing in gains from the earlier rally.

A similar pattern has occurred over several months, with recurring spikes in loss-making exchange transfers as Bitcoin’s price swung higher and lower. The latest red spike appears near the deepest readings visible since July.

A separate CryptoQuant chart breaks down deposits to Binance by the time since each Bitcoin last moved on-chain. It shows 3,290 BTC arriving from coins last moved one day to one week earlier on November 1, followed by a much larger 8,114 BTC from the same category on November 3.

On November 9, the platform also received 1,925 BTC from coins last moved one to three months earlier, according to Taha’s analysis. Those figures help identify which age groups are active, but they do not necessarily reveal when the owners originally purchased their Bitcoin.

The Binance chart measures one exchange and groups coins by their last on-chain movement. The profit-and-loss charts track short-term holders sending coins to exchanges more broadly.

The timing matters because Bitcoin has been sliding from its late-September highs above $85,000 into the $73,000-to-$74,000 area visible at the end of the screenshots. A newer buyer who paid $80,000 would be sitting on a paper loss of roughly 7.5% with Bitcoin at $74,000; selling at that price would lock it in.

The recent weakness is not limited to short-term holders. Glassnode identified about 4 million BTC held by longer-term investors that had been acquired between $85,000 and $118,000, potentially leaving another pocket of underwater supply above current prices.

#5129. FBI warns active $400M crypto scam targets your friends by replacing your face in videos

The FBI says North Korean hackers reuse stolen accounts and webcam footage to draw the next contact into a fake meeting.

North Korean hackers are using stolen webcam recordings to impersonate crypto workers in fake meetings with their contacts, turning one victim's familiar face into bait for the next attack, the FBI warns.

The Justice Department announced disruption of cloud-based infrastructure used in FaceStealer on November 12. It said the scheme had caused more than $400 million in cryptocurrency theft over the preceding 18 months and that the FBI had seized over 900 victim webcam videos under a federal warrant.

The DOJ release treats FaceStealer separately from the Binance theft, which CryptoSlate has covered through the FBI's attribution and the exchange's asset-replenishment delays.

In its November 12 FLASH advisory, the FBI describes attackers taking over genuine accounts on services including Telegram, LinkedIn, Slack and Discord. Access to chat histories lets them tailor an invitation to earlier conversations, giving a new approach the context of an existing relationship.

A legitimate calendaring service can handle the scheduling. The malicious meeting link arrives shortly before the call, directing the target to a copycat Zoom or Microsoft Teams session controlled by the attackers.

Once the target enters, stored webcam footage makes it appear that the known contact has joined. Attackers can simulate several participants. The familiar person on screen can therefore be a real prior victim's recording, rather than a live participant.

The FBI says FaceStealer still overwhelmingly relies on stolen genuine videos. Generated deepfakes provide an additional way to impersonate participants.

The target's webcam becomes part of the attack before the supposed troubleshooting begins. The FLASH says recording starts when the target first clicks the imposter meeting link. The attackers can later use that footage to impersonate the target.

That is where the scheme joins theft to impersonation. Access to the computer can expose cryptocurrency or other valuable access. Stolen communication accounts, contact lists and webcam footage give the hackers material for the next approach. The FBI's FaceStealer resource page describes the same cycle of compromise, account hijacking and fake meetings.

The damage is not necessarily immediate. The FBI reported cases in which cryptocurrency theft and communication-account takeovers came months to more than a year after the initial compromise. A quiet period after a suspicious meeting therefore does not establish that a device or account is safe.

The cycle shows reuse, not a fixed timetable or every encounter. The FBI says genuine stolen footage predominates, while generated deepfakes are also used.

The FBI recommends using the official meeting application with an invite code and, where possible, confirming an invitation through a different communication channel. That checks the approach beyond the account the attacker may already control.

It also advises delaying webcam activation until the inviter can be seen, heard and communicated with. An apparent technical fault should not lead to running scripts or pasting terminal code presented as a video-client update.

For people who suspect compromise, the bureau recommends securing cryptocurrency in a new crypto wallet created on an unaffected device, securing communication and developer accounts, alerting contacts and employers, and reporting to IC3 with the keyword FaceStealer. Alerting contacts can interrupt further approaches that could reuse the stolen account and recording.

#5127. XRP Backer Counters SWIFT’s New Speed Report

Home » Ripple (XRP) » XRP Backer Counters SWIFT’s New Speed Report

The preference for nearly-immediate settlement time windows unites a roster of banks in SWIFT’s chain trial.

A Swift report highlighting faster cross-border payments drew a pointed response from Digital Asset Investor, who replied that he prefers 3-4 seconds and pointed to XRP.

The exchange underscores the ongoing contrast between improvements in traditional interbank messaging and the settlement times associated with blockchain-based rails.

Swift’s Spotlight on Speed report, released this week, shows that 50% of payments on its network now reach the recipient institution within 40 seconds, with 75% arriving within 10 minutes.

What will define the next generation of cross-border payments?The answer? More than just speed.Throughout @Sibos, conversations repeatedly focused on the customer experience. How do we make cross-border transactions more intuitive, more transparent and more predictable for… pic.twitter.com/yZoeZMDN4z

The cooperative noted that these figures put the industry ahead of the G20’s target for one-hour end-to-end processing by 2027 in the interbank leg of the journey.

The same report emphasizes that the “last mile”, the period after a payment reaches the receiving bank and before it is credited to the beneficiary’s account, still accounts for about 80% of the average end-to-end journey time.

Across 40 receiving markets analyzed, median last-mile processing sat near one hour in roughly one-third of cases, with wide variation between cross-border markets.

The conglomerate has called for greater use of one-leg-out models that connect international payments to domestic instant systems to reduce those final delays.

Digital Asset Investor’s reply to the Swift post was brief: “I prefer 3-4 seconds. XRP.” The comment references the XRP Ledger’s typical ledger close time of roughly 3-5 seconds, which provides finality for on-ledger transfers.

I prefer 3-4 seconds. XRP. https://t.co/tBqXtEsqeM

In Ripple’s On-Demand Liquidity (ODL) model, XRP is used as a bridge asset so that currency conversion and settlement can occur without pre-funded nostro accounts.

End-to-end ODL flows that include exchange conversions have been described in the 3-5 second range for the core ledger step, though real-world completion including compliance and local payouts is often measured in seconds to a few minutes depending on the corridor.

The two claims are not measuring identical segments of a payment. Swift’s 40-second figure tracks time to the recipient institution, while the longer last-mile delays occur after that point.

https://t.co/ZA3CcggMOf @swiftcommunity @XRP @realfrandeolza @Archie_XRPL

XRP’s cited 3-4 second window refers primarily to ledger settlement of the bridge asset itself.

Traditional systems still handle the bulk of global bank-to-bank volume and benefit from established compliance and messaging standards; blockchain rails emphasize reduced pre-funding and faster finality on the asset transfer.

Whether the shorter settlement window on XRP produces a meaningfully better end-user experience continues to depend on how the on- and off-ramps, local banking rails, and compliance steps are integrated in any given corridor.

#5126. Stablecoin Drain, ETF Outflows Leave Bitcoin 'Running on Empty'

Stablecoin Drain, ETF Outflows Leave Bitcoin 'Running on Empty'

The pool of dollars that fuels crypto trading is draining.

Total stablecoin supply fell by $14.2 billion over the 30 days through Nov. 9, the fastest contraction since June 2022, according to a report published Wednesday by onchain analytics firm Glassnode.

The total stablecoin supply now sits just below $280 billion, and the research company suggests that's a big reason why Bitcoin is currently "running on empty."

Stablecoins, tokens typically pegged to the U.S. dollar, serve as crypto’s cash. Traders park money in them on exchanges and onchain before buying other assets.

When the stablecoin supply shrinks, it means holders are redeeming tokens for dollars and pulling that money out of crypto entirely, which Glassnode said leaves “less fuel for a rally.” The firm said a return to supply growth would be the first sign that fresh money is coming in.

The stablecoin drain isn’t the only sign of money leaving. U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs saw about $1.6 billion in net redemptions over 20 trading sessions, the report found, and Bitcoin has traded at a discount on Coinbase, a gauge of U.S. demand.

Bitcoin also slipped below the average cost basis of short-term holders, about $75,600, leaving most recent buyers underwater, and traded near $73,000 on Wednesday. Over $3.6 billion in Bitcoin was recently moved over to exchanges, potentially to be sold, at a loss, according to a separate report from CryptoQuant today.

Glassnode did point to some silver linings. The slide has flushed out most leveraged long positions near the current price, buy orders outweigh sell orders in the order book, and wallets holding between 100 and 10,000 BTC have started accumulating.

The firm flagged $73,000 as key support and said the broader trend change that began in August remains intact as long as Bitcoin holds above its June low.

The contraction comes as stablecoins face growing competition from traditional finance.

Global banks including Goldman Sachs, Citi, and Deutsche Bank are backing a $270 million challenge to crypto’s dominant stablecoin issuers, and the Federal Reserve recently unveiled stablecoin rules on reserves and capital.

#5123. XRP loans trigger 883 liquidations, and $53M remains at risk

Morpho liquidators seized 4.18 million cbXRP as XRP-backed borrowers repaid $4 million in debt, with $53.5 million still outstanding.

XRP-backed borrowers surrendered about 4.18 million cbXRP in 883 liquidation events on Morpho, as liquidators repaid just over 4 million USDC of debt.

The activity took place in a lending market on Base where borrowers pledge cbXRP to borrow USDC.

CryptoSlate's analysis of Morpho's indexed transaction records covers Nov. 7 at 10:30:51 UTC through Nov. 13 before 13:00 UTC. The 883 events count individual liquidation logs, so one person can be represented more than once.

A later snapshot on Nov. 13 still showed 53.53 million USDC outstanding.

An earlier loan-stress coverage used Nov. 6 positions to estimate that a further 10% oracle-price decline could bring 8.84 million USDC of debt across 1,070 positions to liquidation eligibility, assuming balances stayed unchanged.

The market's liquidation threshold is 62.5% loan-to-value, which compares the debt with the collateral's value: falling collateral prices can push the same loan above the permitted ratio.

Under Morpho's liquidation mechanism, an outside liquidator can repay some or all of an eligible position's debt and receive collateral plus an incentive. Here, that means paying USDC and taking cbXRP.

Collateral leaves the position while the debt obligation shrinks, and the records alone do not fully capture each borrower's economic outcome.

The largest daily repayment total in the selected window was about 1.58 million USDC on Nov. 8, followed by about 1.06 million on Nov. 10. All 883 selected liquidation records reported zero bad debt, the debt left uncovered by collateral.

The decoded liquidation log for a Nov. 10 transaction shows about 202,394 USDC repaid, and 218,175 cbXRP seized in the same market.

The liquidator then sent that cbXRP amount to another address and received USDC and wrapped ETH from that address in the same transaction. A separate Nov. 7 log records about 1,050 USDC repaid against 1,029 cbXRP seized.

Establishing native XRP selling would require evidence linking the seized collateral to subsequent XRP trading, including any redemption or custody movement along the way.

#5121. Nvidia-Backed CoreWeave Is Surging: Here’s What It Means for the AI Boom

Nvidia-Backed CoreWeave Is Surging: Here’s What It Means for the AI Boom

Nvidia-backed CoreWeave soared 24.7% Wednesday, helping revive the AI trade after weeks of selling, as the company reported surging demand for the expensive computing hardware powering the artificial intelligence boom.

The cloud provider posted $3.66 billion in third-quarter revenue, up 168% from a year ago, and raised its 2026 sales forecast to $13 billion to $13.3 billion. The results also helped lift Nvidia, along with AI infrastructure stocks including Nebius, IREN, Oracle and Applied Digital.

For investors watching Nvidia, CoreWeave offers a useful look at what happens after the chipmaker sells its processors.

CoreWeave buys Nvidia GPUs, installs them in data centers, and rents that computing power to companies developing or running AI models, including OpenAI and other major customers.

That makes its revenue growth evidence that businesses are still willing to pay for AI computing capacity. It does not, by itself, establish that the enormous spending required to supply that capacity will produce sustainable profits.

Nvidia's connection goes well beyond a typical supplier relationship. In January, Nvidia invested another $2 billion in CoreWeave shares at $87.20 each, expanding a business arrangement aimed at building more than five gigawatts of AI data-center capacity by 2030.

The companies also agreed to introduce new Nvidia technology across CoreWeave's infrastructure, including its Rubin platform and Vera CPUs. That makes CoreWeave an important showcase and customer for future Nvidia hardware, not just the chips already installed.

“Together, we’re racing to meet extraordinary demand for NVIDIA AI factories,” Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang said when the expanded deal was announced in January.

Nvidia also has a $6.3 billion initial agreement to buy CoreWeave's unused computing capacity through April 2032, subject to the contract's conditions. In practice, the arrangement gives CoreWeave a buyer for capacity it cannot sell elsewhere, while Nvidia gets access to cloud computing built around its own chips.

The relationship explains both the excitement and some of the criticism surrounding AI investment. Nvidia sells the hardware, invests in a company buying that hardware, and has also committed to purchasing some of the computing services it helps create. Inventors call it “circular finance.” AI bros call it a meme. Skeptics call it a warning sign.

Nvidia gives money to OpenAI who gives money to Coreweave who gives money to Nvidia who gives money to OpenAi who gives money to Coreweave who gives money to OpenAi who gives money to Nvidia pic.twitter.com/3UFfK7KwJv

—  Q-Cap  (@qcapital2020) September 22, 2025

Those are real commercial agreements, but the overlapping financial relationships complicate attempts to measure independent demand.

CoreWeave reported $132.5 billion in revenue backlog, meaning contracted business that it expects to deliver over time, not money already in the bank. The company says it is working with customers including OpenAI, Cohere, and Perplexity, and had more than 1.7 gigawatts of active power capacity at the end of September.

“This was a breakout quarter for CoreWeave, with revenue increasing by more than $1 billion sequentially,” CEO Michael Intrator said in the company's earnings release.

The company also expects about $9 billion in customer prepayments and deposits over the next three months. Getting paid before delivering all the contracted services could reduce its immediate need to borrow at a time when investors have become increasingly uncomfortable with the debt financing AI data centers.

The market reaction extended beyond CoreWeave. Wednesday's rebound touched Nvidia shares and the broader technology market, with the Nasdaq gaining 1.6%. CoreWeave's report arrived as investors were trying to decide whether recent AI-stock losses reflected weakening demand or anxiety about the cost of meeting it.

These specialized GPU-rental businesses are known as neoclouds. Some—including CoreWeave, which began as an Ethereum miner—have roots in crypto infrastructure, where operators were already accustomed to running large amounts of power-hungry hardware.

Bernstein analysts described the quarter as “about the best quarter we could have asked for,” according to Reuters, but warned CoreWeave would be among the companies hit hardest if the shortage of available AI computing capacity begins to ease.

The Nvidia partnership does not remove that risk. Newer processors can make older GPUs less competitive, while electricity availability, construction delays, and higher borrowing costs can all squeeze returns. An oversupply of AI computing would also put pressure on the rental prices CoreWeave earns.

#5116. Diesel prices plunge 8%, yet Bitcoin traders face a squeeze

October’s PPI slowed at the headline level, but higher freight prices and firm underlying inflation leave financing relief uncertain.

US wholesale inflation slowed in October, but rising freight prices and firm underlying pressure complicate the case that cheaper fuel will make financing easier for Bitcoin (BTC) holders while BTC remains below $70,000.

The Bureau of Labor Statistics’ October producer-price report, released Nov. 13, showed diesel prices falling 7.9% as truck freight prices rose 3.9%. Headline wholesale inflation slowed sharply, but the measure excluding food, energy, and trade services kept rising at September’s monthly pace.

Final-demand PPI rose 0.3% in October, seasonally adjusted, after September’s revised 1.4% increase.

The measure excluding food, energy and trade services rose 0.5% for a second month. Its annual increase eased to 4.9% from 5%, while headline annual PPI accelerated to 6.5% from 6.3%. Those readings support a mixed assessment of some comparisons improved, but underlying monthly pressure held firm.

BLS attributed more than 80% of October’s 0.2% rise in final-demand services prices to truck freight. Transportation and warehousing services rose 2%, even as final-demand energy prices slipped 0.1%. Goods prices increased 0.5%.

Cheaper diesel coexisted with higher prices for moving goods. For now, the freight increase undercuts an assumption that a lower fuel bill immediately means cheaper transport.

Unprocessed intermediate goods prices fell 3.1%. Alongside slower monthly headline inflation and the easing annual exclusion measure, that gives the more optimistic interpretation real evidence. The question is whether that cooling broadens and lasts.

Diesel and truck freight moved in opposite directions in October. The inflation picture also changes with the comparison window.

September → October 2026: headline PPI slowed; the measure excluding food, energy and trade services stayed at 0.5%.

September → October 2026: annual headline PPI rose from 6.3% to 6.5%; the exclusion measure eased from 5.0% to 4.9%.

Fuel relief coexists with firm underlying monthly inflation; annual readings are mixed.

PPI series describe different producer prices. Concurrent diesel and freight changes do not establish cause or pass-through timing. Monthly changes are seasonally adjusted; annual changes are unadjusted. PPI is distinct from CPI and PCE.

Reported BLS figures. Main signed bars share a linear −10% to +5% axis. Panel bars start at zero, with monthly scale 0–1.5% and annual scale 0–7%. September monthly figures use the release's revisions. No causal or policy effect is calculated.

PPI series describe different producer prices. Concurrent diesel and freight changes do not establish cause or pass-through timing. Monthly changes are seasonally adjusted; annual changes are unadjusted. PPI is distinct from CPI and PCE.

PPI measures the selling prices domestic producers receive, CPI measures prices paid by consumers, while the Fed targets inflation measured by personal consumption expenditures (PCE).

Thanks for signing up to The Catalyst. Look out for your first daily email. If you already receive it, you’re all set.

The measures overlap in the economic pressures they describe, but their readings are not interchangeable.

Speaking before that day’s CPI release, Fed Governor Christopher Waller leaned toward further tightening through a 25-basis-point December rate increase if conditions developed as expected.

He said a 50-basis-point increase should be considered if October core CPI resembled the previous two readings around 0.3% or higher.

The subsequent CPI report showed a 0.4% monthly headline increase and a third consecutive 0.3% increase excluding food and energy.

The Fed’s explanation of monetary policy describes how policy-rate changes affect short-term interest rates and broader financial conditions. Applied to Bitcoin, the conditional mechanism is that lower financing costs could make borrowed exposure easier to carry, while easier conditions could encourage investors to allocate more to risk.

The route from producer prices to financing relief remains conditional. Persistent inflation could keep policy restrictive even when one fuel price falls, while a recovery case based on financing relief needs evidence beyond cheaper diesel.

Farside Investors' completed Nov. 12 row records US Bitcoin ETF net outflows of $284.1 million, preceding the PPI release.

ETF flows describe one investment channel. Still, completed inflows would provide firmer evidence of buyers returning than an inflation-based expectation alone.

Broader cooling in consumer and producer prices, less restrictive assessments from policymakers and observable financing relief would strengthen the case that fuel declines are becoming useful for Bitcoin holders.

Sustained ETF inflows would add demand evidence, while continued underlying inflation pressure and further withdrawals would keep that case weaker, even if diesel keeps getting cheaper.

#5114. Pressure Mounts on Nvidia's Jensen Huang Amid Reports of Second Affair

Pressure Mounts on Nvidia's Jensen Huang Amid Reports of Second Affair

Nvidia's board is preparing to remove CEO Jensen Huang after reports that he had two extramarital affairs, one with a woman U.S. intelligence believes is a Chinese spy and another with a company executive, The Wall Street Journal reported on Wednesday.

The board was planning to meet as soon as Wednesday to determine Huang's future, according to people familiar with the matter cited by the Journal. It was not immediately clear who would succeed him, the paper said.

The New York Times reported on Wednesday that Huang had an extramarital relationship with Kimberly Powell, Nvidia's vice president of health care, who reports to him, citing five people who worked at the company. The Journal also reported the relationship, citing a person familiar with the matter.

Nvidia's code of conduct tells employees to avoid situations that create conflicts, including personal relationships, according to the Times. When the newspaper reached him by phone, Huang said, "I don't think you should be talking to me directly," before hanging up. Nvidia declined to comment, and Powell did not respond to requests for comment from either paper.

It is the second affair involving Huang to come to light. The New York Times reported in October that U.S. officials had concluded Alice Huang, an executive at Singapore-based Nvidia customer Megaspeed, was a Chinese intelligence asset who had developed a close relationship with Jensen Huang. The Financial Times reported last week that a U.S. government memo said the two had been romantically involved. China has denied the allegations.

On Sunday, Huang acknowledged in a letter to staff that he had been unfaithful to his wife, without naming the person involved. He had told Nvidia's board that he had been intimate with Alice Huang, the Times reported, prompting the board to open an independent investigation, led by law firm Wachtell, Lipton, Rosen & Katz.

The Justice Department is now leading multiple investigations involving Alice Huang, the Journal reported. Huang also faces a proposed shareholder class action and the threat of a congressional subpoena.

Nvidia shares were down 5.9% at $163.43 in premarket trading early on Thursday, according to Yahoo! Finance data, after closing up 2.9% at $173.73 on Wednesday, before the reports emerged. The stock had already lost about $430 billion in market value on Monday and Tuesday.

Traders expect further losses. On Decrypt Predict, users put an 89% chance on Nvidia trading at or below $160 during regular market hours at some point in November, according to the market. By contrast, they gave just a 6% chance that the stock would climb back to $216 this month.

Huang co-founded Nvidia in 1993 and is its largest shareholder, owning about 3.6% of the company. He has said he does not believe in succession planning, according to the Journal, and the company's latest proxy statement warns that it is "highly dependent" on its longstanding executive team, raising questions over who could replace him.

Potential successors are reportedly under discussion already. One person inside the company told the Financial Times that the simplest option would be to appoint chief financial officer Colette Kress as interim CEO, while two sources pointed to Ian Buck, who runs Nvidia's data center business. Analysts cited Arm CEO Rene Haas, a former Nvidia executive, as a possible outside candidate. "We always knew key man risk was an issue for Nvidia," Bernstein analyst Stacy Rasgon told the paper.

At least one high-profile figure has offered Huang a way forward. Responding to a tweet urging him to hire Huang, Tesla CEO Elon Musk wrote: "That would be an honor."

DOJ secured court authority over $1.2 billion from Binance’s $6 billion hack, with forfeiture and repayment timelines unresolved.

US authorities have secured court authorization to seize or restrain more than $1.2 billion stolen from Binance funds, advancing the legal effort to recover assets from the October theft.

The Department of Justice (DOJ) disclosed the authorization on Nov. 12 but did not announce completed forfeiture or a timetable for returning the money.

The court-covered assets sit within more than $2.7 billion frozen through combined US government and private-sector efforts, according to the department.

The larger figure measures the combined freezing effort, while the smaller one identifies the portion for which DOJ reports seizure or restraint authority.

Binance had already committed to covering its losses in its Nov. 3 incident report. The exchange promised to absorb the financial impact of the stolen funds and said it had set aside more than 100% of what it would need to cover the loss.

DOJ attributes the theft of more than $6 billion on or about Oct. 29 to North Korean military actors known as TraderTraitor. Its announcement said efforts to trace, freeze, seize and forfeit the stolen assets remained ongoing as the attackers continued laundering them through cryptocurrency bridges, mixers and exchanges.

#5110. Bitcoin ETFs Bleed $1.4B in Five Days as Investors Cut Risk

Bitcoin ETFs Bleed $1.4B in Five Days as Investors Cut Risk

U.S. spot Bitcoin exchange-traded funds have recorded five consecutive days of net outflows, as investors retreat from risk assets after a turbulent week for markets.

The funds lost some $1.44 billion between November 5 and November 11, including $299.9 million on Wednesday, according to SoSoValue data. That brings net outflows for November so far to $1.88 billion, after $520 million left the funds in October.

The outflows have coincided with a sell-off in AI and technology stocks. On November 5, when the Nasdaq Composite fell 5.5% in a single day, Bitcoin ETFs saw net outflows of about $430 million.

"This wave of outflows is the result of institutional investors actively or passively reducing their risk exposure following a decline in macro risk appetite, which is not yet sufficient to prove that Bitcoin's long-term allocation thesis has reversed," Tim Sun, senior researcher at HashKey, told Decrypt.

The five-day outflows amount to about 2.6% of the funds' $55.1 billion in cumulative net inflows, "far from a full-scale retreat," Sun said. But the funds' total net assets have fallen to $93.7 billion, down about 45% from a peak of $169.5 billion in October 2025, as both outflows and falling prices take their toll.

Bitcoin is trading at $73,358, down 0.87% over the past 24 hours, according to Decrypt data. On Decrypt Predict, users put a 40% chance on Bitcoin trading above $74,000 on Sunday afternoon, and a 94% chance that it will hold above $70,000. Sun estimated that the average holding cost for spot Bitcoin ETFs is around $81,000, meaning some ETF holders are now sitting on unrealized losses, and that some investors may cut their exposure further as they reassess their allocations at year-end.

Analysts say the bigger concern is a shortage of new buyers. In a note shared with Decrypt, Greg Cipolaro, head of research at BitGo, said the post-election bounce brought only $75 million into spot Bitcoin ETFs, while the supply of dollar-pegged stablecoins contracted 1.9% to $286.3 billion, "suggesting little fresh capital is waiting on the sidelines." Onchain analytics firm Glassnode found that total stablecoin supply fell by $14.2 billion in the 30 days through November 9, the fastest contraction since June 2022, Decrypt reported on Wednesday.

The basis trade, in which hedge funds bought spot ETF shares while shorting futures to capture the price gap, has also become less attractive because the basis has fallen below borrowing costs, prompting many funds to exit, Cipolaro said. That means ETF flows may now reflect directional demand for Bitcoin more directly than before, according to Sun.

Corporate buyers have also slowed. The premium of Strategy's stock over the value of its Bitcoin holdings has narrowed, making it less attractive for the company to raise capital to buy more, while MSCI's decision to exclude it from its indexes could cut off passive investment, Sun said.

"The most critical factor to watch right now is the persistent lack of buying demand itself, the impact of which on prices may be more significant than the outflow figures alone," he said.

Cipolaro said Bitcoin had fallen with risk assets but lagged their recoveries. "Unless it begins to participate in rallies and ETF demand strengthens, digital assets could remain exposed to further downside without benefiting from a broader risk asset rebound," he wrote.

Many people forget just how long the 'winter' was for $GLD. It had an initial burst, even becaming the biggest ETF in world for one day in 2011 ,and then the bad times came and and it (saw 40% of investors bail) and took nearly a DECADE to get back to its that aum high again.… pic.twitter.com/Ny9gyyo1Am

— Eric Balchunas (@EricBalchunas) November 11, 2026

Not everyone sees the outflows as a long-term warning sign. Bloomberg ETF analyst Eric Balchunas compared Bitcoin ETFs with gold ETF GLD, which saw around 40% of its investors leave after its 2011 peak and took nearly a decade to recover its assets, but now holds nearly three times that early high. "Assets without cash flows run purely on sentiment and it changes," he wrote.

#5106. Unocoin halts all services after hackers bypass BitGo freeze

Unocoin says suspected misuse of backup wallet access enabled unauthorized transfers outside BitGo as the exchange investigates losses.

Crypto exchange Unocoin said on Nov. 13 that disputed wallet transfers were signed and broadcast outside BitGo, while the freeze on its BitGo enterprise account had worked so far.

The exchange suspended all services on Nov. 9 after detecting further unauthorized activity. It had requested freezes on its enterprise accounts at BitGo and Fireblocks after initially detecting the activity on Nov. 6.

In its incident update, Unocoin said a backup mechanism designed to preserve access to funds if BitGo became unavailable appeared to have been exploited. It is still investigating how that mechanism was used, cryptocurrency losses, and potential information exposure.

BitGo's wallet documentation describes three keys: the user key, backup key, and BitGo key. Normal transactions use the user and BitGo keys to meet a two-of-three signing requirement. The backup key can instead pair with either of the other two keys.

Pairing the backup key with the user key provides a signing route that does not require BitGo's key, and the two-of-three requirement still applies in that recovery arrangement.

What changes is the pair of keys used to satisfy it: the user and backup keys replace the usual user-and-provider combination, leaving BitGo outside that signing process.

BitGo notes that limit in its withdrawal-policy documentation, saying that those policies apply only to transactions involving BitGo. Recovery transactions using the user and backup keys bypass the policies configured with the provider.

The user and BitGo keys sign. BitGo participates, and its withdrawal policies apply.

This recovery capability preserves access when the provider is unavailable and helps explain why an account freeze cannot be treated as a blanket restriction on every transaction the wallet's keys can sign.

Unocoin reported identifying outgoing transactions on Nov. 12 from an Ethereum address within its BitGo wallet infrastructure used to fund ERC-20 tokens. Its Nov. 13 explanation attributes the disputed activity to external signing, while the suspected misuse of backup access remains under investigation.

In the Nov. 12 report, Unocoin said more than 90% of customer cryptocurrency funds were maintained in cold storage. It was still establishing the complete status of holdings and potential exposure, so that statement does not settle the loss assessment.

Unocoin's latest update said work to restore services continued. Unresolved questions include how the suspected recovery path was accessed, what losses or information exposure resulted, and when services can resume.

#5104. India's Financial Crimes Agency Searches CoinDCX, Delta Exchange Over Offshore Trades

India's Financial Crimes Agency Searches CoinDCX, Delta Exchange Over Offshore Trades

India's Enforcement Directorate has searched three premises in Bengaluru linked to crypto exchanges CoinDCX and Delta Exchange, alleging the platforms carried out unauthorized cross-border transactions worth hundreds of millions of dollars through crypto derivatives and tokenized assets.

The searches were carried out on November 4 and 5 under India's Foreign Exchange Management Act (FEMA), the agency, India's main financial crimes investigator, said in a statement dated November 6, which it shared on X on Thursday.

ईडी, बेंगलुरु ने क्रिप्टो टोकन डेरिवेटिव एवं वास्तविक विश्व परिसंपत्ति (आरडब्ल्यूए) टोकन से जुड़े बड़े पैमाने पर अनधिकृत सीमा-पार वित्तीय लेन-देन के मामले में फेमा, 1999 के अंतर्गत मेसर्स नेब्लियो टेक्नोलॉजीज प्राइवेट लिमिटेड (“कॉइनडीसीएक्स”) तथा मेसर्स एक्सेलियम टेक्नोलॉजीज… pic.twitter.com/vXwMU5uCTj

The investigation targets Neblio Technologies, which operates CoinDCX, and Excelium Technologies, which runs Delta Exchange. Both platforms offered futures and options on crypto tokens and openly advertised trading in tokenized shares of foreign companies, despite not being authorized to do so, according to the agency.

The Enforcement Directorate alleged that CoinDCX used stablecoins such as USDT to carry out trades for its users on foreign crypto exchanges, including Binance, KuCoin, Bybit and Gate.io, bypassing India's framework for sending money abroad.

When users deposited rupees and placed spot or derivatives orders, CoinDCX converted the funds into USDT and opened matching positions on the foreign exchanges, the agency said. The trades ran through accounts held in the name of a Costa Rica-based group entity, which it described as a shell entity, and were carried out directly from CoinDCX through APIs.

Trades in tokenized shares of companies such as Apple, Google and Tesla were in fact derivatives positions opened on decentralized exchange Hyperliquid, according to the agency.

The Enforcement Directorate alleged that the cross-border transactions in each of these areas ran to hundreds of millions of dollars. It also said CoinDCX holds crypto assets in enterprise accounts on foreign exchanges, and has paid tens of millions of dollars in fees to those platforms in USDT, in breach of FEMA.

The agency said a large share of Delta Exchange's derivatives trading was executed through CoinDCX, and that Delta Exchange had transferred tens of millions of dollars to its overseas group entities, which is under investigation. Their fintech products also appear to contravene India's securities and central banking laws, it said, adding that its investigation is ongoing.

CoinDCX said in a tweet on November 6 that Enforcement Directorate officials had visited its Bengaluru office "as part of a routine enquiry" on November 4, and that it had fully cooperated. The exchange said it operates "in strict compliance with all applicable Indian laws, including FEMA," and adheres to its KYC, anti-money laundering and reporting obligations as an entity registered with India's Financial Intelligence Unit. Trading, deposits and withdrawals on the platform remain fully operational, it added.

Officials from the Enforcement Directorate visited our Bengaluru office as part of a routine enquiry on 4th November. We fully cooperated with the authorities and provided all necessary information and assistance.

As an entity registered with FIU-IND, we regularly…

Delta Exchange said in its own tweet on November 6 that it had cooperated fully with officials, and that its business "does not involve any cross-border transfer of VDAs in any form or manner," using India's term for crypto assets. It said it runs a dedicated rupee-settled exchange for Indian users only, has been registered with India's Financial Intelligence Unit since 2023, and that trading, deposits and withdrawals were functioning normally.

The investigation adds to a difficult stretch for CoinDCX, one of India's largest crypto exchanges. Last month, it confirmed a $16 million loss from retired wallets, days after co-founder and CEO Sumit Gupta called reports of a breach a "false alarm." That followed a roughly $44 million exploit in July 2025.

Coinbase, which has invested in CoinDCX since 2020, won approval from India's competition regulator to increase its minority stake in the exchange's parent company.

#5100. Morning Minute: Tokenized Stock Venues Are Launching Without Big Tech’s Approval

Morning Minute: Tokenized Stock Venues Are Launching Without Big Tech’s Approval

Morning Minute is a daily newsletter written by Tyler Warner. The analysis and opinions expressed are his own and do not necessarily reflect those of Decrypt. And check out our daily news show 'FOMO HOUR' covering all of the top stories and market action.

🏛️ OKX’s Tokenized Stock Venue Launches Without Big Tech

In September, after the CLARITY Act died in the Senate, the SEC created an innovation exemption letting venues trade tokenized versions of US stocks without waiting for new legislation. It came with one condition. A company that doesn’t want a third party minting tokens of its shares can object in writing within 30 days, and that’s the end of it.

Companies have been objecting ever since. The count at the OKXICE venue went from 22 in October to 50, then 56, and as of its November 5 notice, 67. Every member of the Magnificent Seven is on that list.

OKXICE is launching anyway, on November 23. The venue will list more than 70 assets, though 59 of them are Direxion ETFs. The individual stocks that made it through are Coinbase, Circle, Robinhood, Strategy, BitGo, Securitize and Better.com. Strategy is also tokenizing its preferred shares.

Securitize handles the tokenization, each token is backed one-for-one by a real share and carries dividends and voting rights, and trading runs through Uniswap v4 pools on X Layer, OKX’s Ethereum layer-2.

So a venture between a global exchange and the parent of the New York Stock Exchange built a tokenized equities market, and what it opens with is seven crypto companies and a series of leveraged ETFs.

Notably, this news comes just a day after the NYSE picked Avalanche to handle clearing and settlement for its own 24/7 tokenized securities platform, with a fourth-quarter target for launch after about a year of testing. The NYSE has signed agreements with Broadridge, Computershare, Equiniti and Superstate to support issuer-sponsored tokenized securities and transfer-agent functions. When the company’s own share registry issues the token, there is nothing to veto.

DTCC is doing a version of this too, with a tokenization service that went live October 28 on the Canton Network carrying 20 participants including Bank of America, Citi, JPMorgan and Citadel Securities. Morgan Stanley has already run equities and Treasuries through it.

Progress is being made, slowly but surely. It just gets built slowly, through transfer agents and clearing houses, by the incumbents. Now we wait to see how the market reacts to these first launches…
